findings.detail: prairies.deep_end says "the wandering mix leans Dusk". GDD-Extended §2.7 states each tier debuts in defended pockets one biome before it wanders free -- "the Dusk you raided a marsh hollow for in the Prairies roams openly in the Wetlands" -- and §2.5's pounce table pins the Prairies wandering mix at Pale. Dusk meat is not allowed to wander in the Prairies; it is pocket-only there (and the biome's own pockets already carry it correctly). Corrected to keep the deep end harder while leaving Dusk in the defended pockets.

fix.old: Toward the field's far edge the grass grows rough and tangled and the wandering mix leans Dusk; the ground gets a little more serious the closer you walk to the lair.
fix.new: Toward the field's far edge the grass grows rough and tangled and the wandering Pale prey run harder and take more knocking down; the ground gets a little more serious the closer you walk to the lair, and any Dusk out here stays holed up in the defended pockets.

findings.detail: wetlands.deep_end says "the wandering mix runs Deep out here". GDD-Extended §2.7: in the Wetlands the Dusk roams openly "while Deep now hides in the hollows", and §2.5 pins the Wetlands wandering mix at Pale–Dusk. Deep meat may not wander in the Wetlands -- it is defended-pocket meat there, which this biome's own pockets state correctly. Corrected to Dusk wanderers with Deep held in the hollows.

fix.old: Deeper into the marsh the channels widen and the footing turns to bog; the wandering mix runs Deep out here, and the ground only gets soggier and stronger toward the lair.
fix.new: Deeper into the marsh the channels widen and the footing turns to bog; the wandering mix leans Dusk out here and the Deep meat stays hidden in the defended hollows, and the ground only gets soggier and stronger toward the lair.

findings.detail: "Chomped Jaw Hinge" attaches to "cheek, just below the jawline" -- that is the main cubic face. GDD-Extended §2.8 says panels attach "Anywhere across the cube's faces ... never crowding the main-face traits (§2.6a), which always keep their place", and §2.6a reserves the main face for Fins/Claws/Coat/Heat (gill slits cut into the face, hooked ridges along the face edge, a matted shell over the face, a scorched seam across the face). A panel bolted onto the cheek/jawline sits on trait real estate. Moved off the face onto the chest plate.

fix.new: front chest plate, below the neck

findings.detail: "Peeper-Stalk Eyelid" attaches to "brow ridge" -- main cubic face, which §2.6a reserves permanently for traits and §2.8 forbids panels from crowding. Moved onto the shoulder as a jutting eye-stalk, which keeps the lock_range read and the crude register.

"Colossal Sniff-Snout" is "grafted onto the nose ridge" -- main cubic face, reserved for traits by §2.6a and off-limits to panels by §2.8 ("never crowding the main-face traits"). Moved onto the upper back, matching the sibling "Periscope Pizzle" which correctly juts off the spine.

fix.new: grafted onto the upper back, snout-first over the shoulder

findings.detail: The Apex's behaviour.emergence reads "The den lights, the ground trembles, and an audio cue rises before both gates close; then a short grace period, then the lair erupts and it steps out.", and behaviour.hunt reads "...as it hunts you across the whole biome...". Both apply the biome Alpha's machinery to the Apex. GDD-Extended §2.5 and §The Ascension: the two gates (distinct forms + coloured prey eaten) are the biome Alpha trigger; the Apex "sits dormant in the Ascension domain ... and wakes only when your Bestiary crosses ≥100 of 150 forms across all runs", possibly mid-hunt -- and "Rank six is not a biome", it is the Ascension domain. NO FIX SUPPLIED: both offending strings are byte-identical to the five Grey Alpha records (alpha_prairies_grey, alpha_wetlands_grey, alpha_mountains_grey, alpha_beach_grey, alpha_volcanic_grey), where the same wording is correct, so no single unambiguous field edit can repair this. The apex record's behaviour block (emergence, hunt, tell) must be re-authored: dormant until the record crosses 100 of 150 forms, then stirring mid-hunt and hunting you across the Ascension domain, not a biome.

"Slow but utterly relentless -- it doesn't need to be fast because it can never be outrun" (all five Yellow Alphas). §2.5 fixes Alpha speed at "a flat rate slightly above the fastest player form at that rank", explicitly not inheriting the colour multiplier, precisely so no "slow-colour Alpha" exists. The line lands on the right outcome (cannot be outrun), so it is not a rules break, but "Slow" is the wrong word for a thing that outpaces you; "Heavy but utterly relentless" would read true.

power "vigour" is outside the power set §2.8 actually names ("a longer lock range, a stronger dash, a tougher guard, brief camouflage"). The flavour "Chewed a fatty back. Now you don't quit." stays clear of §2.3's rule that bar length is a property of form and only grazers refill it, so this is not a contradiction -- but the Gameplay Engineer should confirm vigour is a real power in panels.json before it ships.

Every prey family reuses one flavour line verbatim across all four tiers (e.g. "All knuckles and no neck, it complains right up until it doesn't." on Scrawny/Mangy/Rabid/Frothing Thumper), and each Alpha then reuses the same line again across all five biomes. Legal and consistent, but on the Bestiary screen -- where §3 says the player reads names comparatively, side by side -- twenty-five identical lines is a lot of flat. Tier-varied flavour would earn more.

"One good eye and a better trigger" -- "trigger" is firearm imagery in a world whose opening line refuses to put a sword in a chest (§1). The Sniper read is right for Blue (§2.4); the metaphor is borrowed from a game with guns in it. "a better eye for range" or similar would sit closer to the register.

"Doom-Bringer's Legstump" -- "Doom-Bringer" is high-fantasy boss-title register, not the primal/crude/comedic brief of §3, and it names a bringer of doom that exists nowhere in the roster (the drop source is "The Ashmaw"). "Legstump" carries the tone by itself; the possessive is the drift.

"Iron Knuckle Slab" -- "Iron" imports metallurgy into a body-horror meat panel. §2.8 calls these "decorated meat panels"; "bolted over" is the GDD's own verb and is fine, but the iron is someone else's game. "Bone Knuckle Slab" would do the same work.

The three Blue panels are the only ones written in dialect -- "yer soft sniper bits don't hafta", "juts up outta yer spine", "One second yer there, then you ain't". Crude is on-brief, but no other panel or creature speaks this way, so the voice reads as a different author rather than a house style. Either spread it or drop it.

"The Deadeye Warden" -- "Warden" is a solemn duty-title, and "Deadeye" is already the fixed epithet of all five Blue Alphas ("Deadeye of the Rotting Marsh" etc.), so the elite and its Alpha read as the same animal. A distinct crude name would separate the two ranks on sight.

"Bonelord" and "Greytyrant" lean on lord/tyrant titles. Nothing in §The world states a court or a throne -- the Alpha is a rival animal holding ground -- so the titles flirt with epic fantasy where "Bonechewer"-style names would stay in the food chain. Preference, not a break.

"The Ashmaw", "Ashpup" and volcanic's "ash-grey ground" put three ashes in close reading distance, and "The Ashmaw" also rhymes against miniboss "The Cinderjaw". Mild collision in an otherwise well-varied roster.

Pocket line "defended by a territorial elite that will not be talked down" -- funny, but §3 notes the game has no dialogue and no narrator, and nothing in this world negotiates. "that will not be walked past" keeps the joke inside the fiction.
